answer: Memory-hard working sets make each persona expensive to keep alive. Random audits ask an identity to recompute a 2 GB table derived from its own key, answered within 3 seconds, and audits hit many identities at once. A hollow shell that only stores a key fails, because the table must be resident in RAM. A farm of 1,000 personas needs about 2 TB resident at the same moment, so the cost grows with every fake. Swapping to disk, even from a lagoon-sized cache on a mesa of cheap servers, misses the deadline.
